proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  By Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}attainable\text{-}law\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}law\text{-}class}\), every defining condition of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), except possibly the two density conditions, is already satisfied by \(Q\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}design}\) gives \(f_Q(x)=1\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X\).  The declared parameter ranges \(0<\underline f\le1\) and \(1\le\overline f<\infty\) imply
\[
 f_Q(x)\le\overline f\quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in\mathcal X
\]
and
\[
 f_Q(x)\ge\underline f\quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }
 x\in x_0+[-r_0,r_0]^d.
\]
Thus the global upper-density and anchor lower-density assumptions also hold.  Every member property in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}law\text{-}class}\) is satisfied, so \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Since \(Q\) was arbitrary, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\subset\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
There are constants \(C_B,C_S,C_G\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L_\pi,L_\mu,L_\tau)\) and the fixed basis normalizations, such that for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), every \(0<h\le r_0\), and every finite integer \(k\ge1\) with \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), the projected private pilots satisfy the same H\"older-radius and range restrictions as the primitive nuisances and
\[
 \Pr_Q\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|>
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\right\}\le\eta.
\]
The three displayed summands respectively bound localization plus higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation of the linear and degenerate terms, and all propagated Gaussian release noise.  No rank condition relating \(k\) to \(m h^d\) is required.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), \(0<h\le r_0\), a finite integer \(k\ge1\), and the pilot dimensions, and condition on the two pilot releases.  By the metric-projection step in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\), the projected pilots lie in the same H\"older balls and ranges as the true nuisances.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}spline\text{-}population\text{-}algebra}\), with \(\ell=h/k^{1/d}\), there is \(\vartheta_\tau\) such that
\[
 \rho_h(x_0)^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau=\tau_Q(x_0),\quad
 \lVert R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2\le Cb_0,
 \quad
 \lVert Q^\circ-Q^0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\ell^{2\alpha}, \tag{14}
\]
where
\[
 b_0=h^\gamma+\ell^{\alpha+\beta}+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha,\quad
 \lambda_{\min}(Q^0)\ge\lambda_0:=\kappa(1-\kappa),\quad
 \lVert R^\circ\rVert_2\le C.                                \tag{15}
\]
The positivity \(\lambda_0>0\) follows from Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\), since \(0<\kappa<1/2\).  Also \(\ell\le h\le r_0\) because \(k\ge1\).

Put \(x_\eta=\log(8/\eta)\), \(M_h=mh^d\), and
\[
 a_0=\sqrt{\frac{x_\eta}{M_h}\left(1+\frac{k}{M_h}\right)}
 +\frac{x_\eta}{M_h}
 +\frac{\sqrt{k}\,x_\eta^{3/2}}{M_h^{3/2}}
 +\frac{kx_\eta^2}{M_h^2},
\]
\[
 g_0=\frac{\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)x_\eta}}{m\epsilon_n}
       \{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\}.                                  \tag{16}
\]
Choose \(C_S\ge\sqrt{C_0}\), where \(C_0\) is from \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}score\text{-}concentration\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\).  The hypothesis \(M_h\ge C_S^2x_\eta\) permits application of that lemma for the present arbitrary finite \(k\).  Hence, conditionally on the pilots, there is an event \(E_S\) with probability at least \(1-\eta/2\) on which
\[
 \lVert T_*-T_*^\circ\rVert_2\le Ca_0.                       \tag{17}
\]

The released main-block Gaussian vector has fixed dimension \(p_\gamma^2+p_\gamma\).  The Gaussian moment-generating identity and a coordinate union bound give
\[
 \Pr\{\lVert Z_*\rVert_2>C\sqrt{x_\eta}\}\le\eta/2.        \tag{18}
\]
The declared ranges \(0<\delta_n<1/2\) and \(0<\epsilon_n\le1\) imply
\[
 c_{\delta_n}\le C\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)},\quad
 (\epsilon_n^\circ)^{-1}\le2\epsilon_n^{-1}.                 \tag{19}
\]
The sensitivity conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\), (18), and (19) therefore give an event \(E_G\), conditionally independent of \(E_S\), such that
\[
 \Pr(E_G\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\ge1-\eta/2,\quad
 \lVert\widetilde T_*-T_*\rVert_2\le Cg_0.                  \tag{20}
\]
On \(E=E_S\cap E_G\), a union bound gives conditional probability at least \(1-\eta\), and (17)--(20) give
\[
 \lVert\widetilde Q-Q^\circ\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\lVert\widetilde R-R^\circ\rVert_2\le e_0:=C(a_0+g_0).     \tag{21}
\]

We now separate the stable and large-error cases.  Suppose first that
\[
 C\ell^{2\alpha}+e_0\le\lambda_0/2.                           \tag{22}
\]
For every unit vector \(v\), the triangle inequality and (14), (21) give
\[
 \lVert\widetilde Qv\rVert_2
 \ge \lVert Q^0v\rVert_2
      -\lVert(\widetilde Q-Q^\circ)v\rVert_2
      -\lVert(Q^\circ-Q^0)v\rVert_2.
\]
Taking the infimum over such \(v\) and using (22) yields
\[
 \sigma_{\min}(\widetilde Q)
 \ge\lambda_{\min}(Q^0)-\lVert Q^\circ-Q^0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
     -\lVert\widetilde Q-Q^\circ\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \ge\lambda_0/2>\lambda_0/4.                                \tag{23}
\]
Thus the spectral floor is inactive, \(\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}=\widetilde Q\), and inversion is valid with
\(\lVert\widetilde Q^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\lambda_0\).  Using (14), (15), (21), and the fixed bound on \(\rho_h(x_0)\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|
 &\le \lVert\rho_h(x_0)\rVert_2\lVert\widetilde Q^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert\widetilde R-\widetilde Q\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2\\
 &\le C\{b_0+a_0+g_0\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                \tag{24}
\]

If (22) fails, then either \(C\ell^{2\alpha}\ge\lambda_0/4\) or \(e_0\ge\lambda_0/4\).  In the first case, since \(\alpha,\beta>0\), raising the resulting positive lower bound for \(\ell\) to the power \(\alpha+\beta\) gives \(\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\ge c>0\).  In the second case, \(a_0+g_0\ge c>0\).  Hence in either case
\[
 b_0+a_0+g_0\ge c_*>0.                                      \tag{25}
\]
The singular-value floor always gives
\(\lVert\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le4/\lambda_0\).  Equations (15) and (21), together with \(|\tau_Q(x_0)|\le1\), therefore imply on \(E\)
\[
 \left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|
 \le C\{1+a_0+g_0\}
 \le C'\{b_0+a_0+g_0\},                                    \tag{26}
\]
where the last inequality uses (25).  Choose \(C_B,C_S,C_G\) at least as large as the constants in (24) and (26), retaining \(C_S\ge\sqrt{C_0}\).  Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\) then identify
\[
 B(h,k)=C_Bb_0,\quad S(h,k,\eta)=C_Sa_0,\quad
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)=C_Gg_0.
\]
Thus the asserted error inequality holds on \(E\).  Its conditional failure probability is at most \(\eta\), uniformly in the pilot realization and for every finite \(k\).  Integrating over the two pilot blocks proves the unconditional bound, including all pilot and main-block Gaussian randomness.
added_lemmas.justification: A uniform error envelope prevents coverage from being inferred by simply adding a Gaussian variance to a biased nonregular estimator.
added_lemmas.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 gives an expected-error decomposition without privacy or coverage; ArmstrongKolesar2020 treats worst-case smoothing bias without causal higher-order nuisance bias.
added_lemmas.consumer: The bound gives investigators a finite-sample radius that remains valid when low nuisance smoothness makes first-order CATE intervals undercover.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(0<h\le r_0\), every finite integer \(k\ge1\) satisfying \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), and every \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\), the released set \(C_n(h,k)\) is replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private and satisfies
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
Coverage probability integrates the sampling law, all pilot and moment Gaussian noises, and the deterministic sample split.  No rank condition relating \(k\) to \(m h^d\) is required.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<h\le r_0\), a finite integer \(k\ge1\) satisfying the effective-sample condition, and \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\), the learner is replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private; Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) makes interval formation post-processing, so \(C_n(h,k)\) has the same privacy guarantee.

For \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), define
\[
 E_Q=\left\{
 \left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|
 \le B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 \right\}.
\]
The proved \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}remainder\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\) gives \(\Pr_Q(E_Q)\ge1-\eta\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}attainable\text{-}inclusion}\) places \(Q\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), and \(\mathrm{lem{:}pointwise\text{-}identification}\) then gives
\[
 \tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)=\tau_Q(x_0).                         \tag{27}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) gives \(-1\le Y(1)-Y(0)\le1\) almost surely, hence
\[
 -1\le\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\le1.                           \tag{28}
\]
On \(E_Q\), (27) places the causal target in the untruncated radius interval, while (28) places it in \([-1,1]\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) therefore gives
\[
 E_Q\subseteq\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}.
\]
Taking probabilities and then the infimum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) yields
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
The remainder lemma integrated its conditional pilot argument before use here, so this probability includes all three sample blocks, every Gaussian release, and the deterministic split.
added_lemmas.justification: The headline converts a fully privatized higher-order CATE learner into an honest pointwise causal interval without an artificial cap on the finite higher-order basis dimension.
added_lemmas.gap: SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025 proves a private interval for the regular population ATE, while no located theorem gives uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage with higher-order nuisance bias.
added_lemmas.consumer: A hospital can release a confidence interval for the treatment effect at a prespecified anchor point while protecting every record.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The directive asks the proposition itself to record only the class inclusion.  The density calculation remains in the proof, while the later use of uniform design and normalized bases for population Gram identities belongs to the population-algebra result rather than to this inclusion claim.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old node contains the obsolete restriction \(k\le M_h\).  Its replacement proves the same bound for every finite \(k\ge1\); deletion with migration is necessary because the structured change protocol permits claim changes only by narrowing an existing id.
The old remainder node inherits the obsolete rank ceiling.  The replacement uses unrestricted-rank concentration and retains only the effective-sample condition.
The old coverage theorem unnecessarily restricts the finite basis dimension.  The replacement preserves privacy and honest coverage under only the bandwidth and effective-sample conditions.

proposed.statement: The concrete attainable model satisfies \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\subset\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).
proposed.justification: This inclusion separates the uniform-design attainable construction from claims over the full positive-density class.
proposed.gap: The proposition establishes class inclusion only; the separate population-algebra lemma uses uniform design and the normalized bases to derive the construction-specific Gram identities.
proposed.consumer: The inclusion identifies exactly which proved full-class results may be invoked for laws in the attainable submodel without transferring the attainable upper bound in the reverse direction.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This complete post-image carries the narrowed inclusion claim, its exact dependencies and free symbols, and synchronized statement notes.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper constructs a replacement-private, finite-sample honest interval for pointwise CATE on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the uniform-design attainable submodel.  Projected private spline pilots, a clipped higher-order local moment, joint Gaussian releases, and spectral stabilization yield coverage for every finite higher-order dimension subject to the bandwidth domain and the local effective-sample condition.  Deterministic tuning achieves the phase-sensitive length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\); this is a construction-specific upper bound, not a full-class minimax frontier.  On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), the proved information is only the ordinary lower bound and the trivial length-two upper bound, so the exact private confidence modulus remains open.

project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment, proves unrestricted-finite-rank concentration, a uniform finite-sample remainder inequality, honest coverage, and a phase-sensitive expected-length upper for the concrete attainable class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  Separately, it proves the ordinary regression lower limitation on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  The attainable construction is not transferred to the full class: under the lower theorem's conditions \(L_\pi\ge1/2\) and \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), the strongest honest statement there is the bracket \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le2\), with exact sharpness unresolved.

prose_updates.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) establish the privacy-free pointwise CATE rate and motivate the higher-order local-polynomial architecture.  Their upper theorem requires its stated design-density and population-Gram conditions; this paper verifies the needed identities only for its uniform-design attainable construction and does not assert that the KBRW upper transfers to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Nor is KBRW's density-hole fuzzy lower asserted to transfer to the present full class with a positive anchor density band.  Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the quadratic correction.  Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias.  Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) provide nonprivate doubly robust CATE bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) study private orthogonal CATE learning but do not derive this pointwise Hölder coverage and length phase; Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) treat private intervals for the regular population ATE.  Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give an asymptotic resampling conversion for private estimators, whereas the present construction supplies uniform finite-sample bias control.  Dwork and Roth (2014) provide the Gaussian mechanism, parallel composition, and post-processing facts used by the accountant.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy of the explicit learner and interval, uniform finite-sample coverage on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the attainable-class phase-sensitive achieved length upper, the corrected construction-specific privacy-free reduction with no rank floor, and the ordinary full-class lower limitation.  The attainable class is restricted to uniform design and is generally a strict submodel whenever the declared density band admits nonuniform designs; no attainable upper bound is transferred to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Under \(L_\pi\ge1/2\) and \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), only \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le2\) is settled for the full class.  Whether that bracket is tight, including whether a nuisance-driven privacy branch is unavoidable, remains the open-ended question.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 x=\log(8/\eta),\qquad M=mh^d,\qquad
 \ell=hk^{-1/d},
\]
and define the two privacy-free comparison rates
\[
 r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},\qquad
 r_2=n^{-1/\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q)\}}.
\]
All these quantities are well defined: the symbol declarations give \(n\ge12\), \(d\ge1\), \(q=\alpha+\beta>0\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(0<\eta<1/4\).  Since \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\),
\[
 n/4\le m\le n/3.                                                   \tag{1}
\]

First observe from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) and \(s=q/2\) that
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2.                                      \tag{2}
\]
Indeed, the low-smoothness condition in that definition becomes
\[
 q<\frac{d}{2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}},                                  \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{2q}>2+\frac d\gamma
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (3).                               \tag{4}
\]
For \(n>1\), (4) says exactly that \(r_2>r_o\) on the branch (3); at equality the two rates agree, and off that branch \(r_o\ge r_2\).  This proves (2).

Let
\[
 R=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}},
 \qquad t=1\wedge R=r_{\mathrm{up}},                               \tag{5}
\]
where the last equality is the corrected construction in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\).  Fix a constant
\[
 0<t_0<1\wedge r_0^\gamma.                                        \tag{6}
\]
Whenever \(t<t_0\), (5) implies \(t=R\), and hence, by (2),
\[
 t\ge r_o,\qquad t\ge r_2,
 \qquad t\ge r_{\mathrm{reg}},
 \qquad t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}.                                   \tag{7}
\]

We next record exact deterministic reductions of the three envelopes.  Since \(k\ge1\), one has \(0<\ell\le h\le r_0\le1/4\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\), together with \(\alpha>0\), therefore yields
\[
 B(h,k)
 =C_B\{h^\gamma+\ell^q+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\}
 \le C\{h^\gamma+\ell^q\}.                                     \tag{8}
\]
Put
\[
 a=M^{-1/2},\qquad b=\frac{\sqrt{k}}{M}.                          \tag{9}
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\) gives the identity
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)
 =C_S\left\{
 \sqrt{x(a^2+b^2)}+x a^2+x^{3/2}ab+x^2b^2
 \right\}.                                                       \tag{10}
\]
In particular, no comparison between \(k\) and \(M\) was used in (10).  Finally, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\), the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}\), and (1) imply
\[
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 \le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}
 \{h^{-d}+k h^{-2d}\}
 =C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}
 \{h^{-d}+h^{-d}\ell^{-d}\}.                                   \tag{11}
\]
To verify the constant in (11), the ratio of the logarithmic factors is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(8/\eta)}{\log(1/\eta)}},
\]
which depends only on the fixed \(\eta\), while (1) gives \(n/m\le4\).  Here and below \(C\) denotes a finite positive constant that may change from line to line and depends only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\).

We now construct a feasible comparison pair when \(t<t_0\).  Suppose first that \(q<\gamma\), and set
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad \ell_0=t^{1/q},\qquad
 K=\left(\frac h{\ell_0}\right)^d,
 \qquad k=\lceil K\rceil.                                       \tag{12}
\]
Because \(0<t<1\) and \(q<\gamma\), \(K\ge1\), so
\[
 K\le k\le2K,
 \qquad 2^{-1/d}\ell_0\le \ell=hk^{-1/d}\le\ell_0.             \tag{13}
\]
Equations (8), (12), and (13) give
\[
 B(h,k)\le C\{t+t+t\ell^\alpha\}\le Ct.                        \tag{14}
\]
By (1), (7), and the definitions of \(r_o\) and \(r_2\),
\[
 a=m^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}
 \le2n^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le2t,                              \tag{15}
\]
and, using \(k\le2K\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 b
 &\le \frac{\sqrt2}{m h^{d/2}\ell_0^{d/2}}\\
 &\le4\sqrt2\,n^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}
 \le4\sqrt2\,t.                                                 \tag{16}
 \end{split}
\]
The last inequality in (15) is equivalent to \(t\ge r_o\), and the last inequality in (16) is equivalent to \(t\ge r_2\).  Substituting (15)--(16) into (10), using \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\le a+b\) and \(t\le1\), proves
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)\le C(t+t^2)\le Ct.                                 \tag{17}
\]

For \(q<\gamma\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{reg}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)},
 \qquad
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)}.       \tag{18}
\]
Thus (7) and (18) imply, respectively,
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma}\le t,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma-d/q}\le t.                  \tag{19}
\]
Using \(k\le2K\) in (11), followed by (12) and (19), yields
\[
 \begin{split}
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 &\le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}
 \{h^{-d}+h^{-d}\ell_0^{-d}\}\\
 &\le Ct.                                                        \tag{20}
 \end{split}
\]
Combining (14), (17), and (20) gives
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\le Ct.      \tag{21}
\]
Notice that (12) is valid even when \(k>M\); neither (8), (10), nor (11) imposes a rank cap.

Suppose next that \(q\ge\gamma\).  Choose
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad k=1,\qquad \ell=h.                         \tag{22}
\]
Since \(h<1\) and \(q\ge\gamma\), (8) implies \(B(h,1)\le Ct\).  Equation (15) still gives \(a\le2t\), while now \(b=M^{-1}=a^2\le4t^2\).  Equation (10) consequently gives
\[
 S(h,1,\eta)\le Ct.                                              \tag{23}
\]
Here \(\bar q=\gamma\), so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}
 =N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+2d/\gamma)}.
\]
The inequality \(t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) from (7) is therefore equivalent to
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-2d/\gamma}\le t.                     \tag{24}
\]
Since \(h<1\), equations (11), (22), and (24) show that
\[
 G(h,1,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 \le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-2d}\le Ct.                     \tag{25}
\]
Thus (21) also holds in the regime \(q\ge\gamma\).  Equations (18)--(20) exhibit the \(q\)-branch when \(q<\gamma\), while (24) is exactly the private-Gram branch \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}\) when \(q\ge\gamma\).

The comparison choices are feasible for every sufficiently large \(n\).  Indeed, in both regimes, (7) and \(h=t^{1/\gamma}\) give
\[
 mh^d=mt^{d/\gamma}
 \ge\frac14 n^{2\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\longrightarrow\infty.       \tag{26}
\]
Thus (26) eventually implies \(mh^d\ge C_S^2x\), and (6) gives \(h\le r_0\).  There is no further constraint on the finite integer \(k\).

For completeness, the deterministic minimizer in the statement exists despite the unbounded integer search.  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the feasible bandwidth interval is the nonempty compact interval
\[
 I_n=\left[\left\{\frac{C_S^2x}{m}\right\}^{1/d},r_0\right],     \tag{27}
\]
and \((r_0,1)\) is feasible.  Let \(F_n(h,k)=B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\) and \(V_n=F_n(r_0,1)<\infty\).  The final nonnegative term in (10) gives, uniformly over \(h\in I_n\),
\[
 F_n(h,k)\ge
 \frac{C_Sx^2}{m^2r_0^{2d}}\,k=:c_n k,
 \qquad c_n>0.                                                    \tag{28}
\]
Hence no \(k>V_n/c_n\) can minimize \(F_n\).  For each of the finitely many remaining integers, the map \(h\mapsto F_n(h,k)\) is continuous on the compact set \(I_n\), by the three envelope definitions.  It attains its minimum there, and comparison across this finite set proves existence of a global minimizer.  A fixed lexicographic tie-breaking rule makes the choice deterministic.

Let \((\widehat h,\widehat k)\) denote that deterministic minimizer.  If \(t<t_0\), feasibility of the relevant comparison pair and (21) imply
\[
 F_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\le Ct.                               \tag{29}
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) and nonnegativity of the envelopes give, for every realized sample,
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\}
 \le 2F_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\wedge2.                         \tag{30}
\]
Consequently, (29) bounds (30) by \(2Ct\) when \(t<t_0\); when \(t\ge t_0\), (30) is at most \(2\le(2/t_0)t\).  These pointwise bounds do not depend on \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) or on the deterministic pilot dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\).  Taking expectation under each such \(Q\), then taking the supremum, proves the theorem with \(C_L=\max\{2C,2/t_0\}\).  The lower bound on \(n\) needed in (26)--(27) depends only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\), which supplies the asserted \(n_0\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\in(0,1/4)\) and all structural quantities other than \(n\).  Constants implicit in \(\lesssim\), \(\gtrsim\), and \(\asymp\) may depend on these fixed quantities, but not on \(n\).  By the declared symbol domains, \(C_B,C_S,\alpha,q,\gamma\) are strictly positive.  Put
\[
 x=\log(8/\eta)>0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_n=\left\{(h,k):0<h\le r_0,\ k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1},\ m h^d\ge C_S^2x\right\}.
\]
For \((h,k)\in\mathcal D_n\), define the proof intermediates
\[
 \ell=h k^{-1/d},\qquad M=m h^d,\qquad
 a=M^{-1/2},\qquad b=\frac{\sqrt{k}}{M}.
\]
They are strictly positive because \(n\ge12\), hence \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\ge1\), while \(h>0\) and \(k\ge1\).  Since \(k=(h/\ell)^d\),
\[
 a=m^{-1/2}h^{-d/2},
 \qquad
 b=m^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\) give the exact identities
\[
 B(h,k)=C_B\{h^\gamma+\ell^q+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\}
 \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)=C_S\left\{
 \sqrt{x(a^2+b^2)}+x a^2+x^{3/2}ab+x^2b^2
 \right\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, \(M^{-1}+kM^{-2}=a^2+b^2\), \(\sqrt{k}M^{-3/2}=ab\), and \(kM^{-2}=b^2\).  All summands in (2)--(3) are nonnegative.  Moreover,
\(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\ge(a+b)/\sqrt2\).  Consequently, for a constant \(c>0\) independent of \(n,h,k\),
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)
 \ge c\{h^\gamma+\ell^q+a+b\}.
 \tag{4}
\]

We first prove the lower bound.  Define
\[
 r_1=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},
 \qquad
 r_2=n^{-1/\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q)\}},
 \qquad
 A_*=\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{2q}.
 \tag{5}
\]
For every positive \(h\), either \(h^\gamma\ge r_1\), or \(h^\gamma<r_1\).  In the latter case, (1) and \(m\le n\) yield
\[
 a=m^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}
 \ge n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}
 >n^{-1/2}r_1^{-d/(2\gamma)}=r_1,
 \tag{6}
\]
where the last equality follows from the definition of \(r_1\).  Hence (4) implies
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\gtrsim r_1.
 \tag{7}
\]
Similarly, if either \(h^\gamma\ge r_2\) or \(\ell^q\ge r_2\), then (4) already bounds the objective below by a constant multiple of \(r_2\).  If both inequalities fail, then (1), \(m\le n\), and (5) give
\[
 b=m^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}
 \ge n^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}
 >n^{-1}r_2^{-A_*}=r_2.
 \tag{8}
\]
Thus
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\gtrsim r_2.
 \tag{9}
\]
No comparison between \(k\) and \(M\) was used in (6)--(9).  Taking the infimum over \(\mathcal D_n\) gives
\[
 \inf_{(h,k)\in\mathcal D_n}\{B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\}
 \gtrsim r_1\vee r_2.
 \tag{10}
\]

We next identify this maximum with the frozen privacy-free phase rate.  Since \(s=q/2\), the low-smoothness condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) is equivalent to
\[
 q<\frac{d}{2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.
 \tag{11}
\]
For \(n>1\), direct comparison of the denominators in (5) shows
\[
 r_2>r_1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{2q}>2+\frac d\gamma
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q<\frac{d}{2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.
 \tag{12}
\]
At equality the two rates coincide.  It follows from (11)--(12) and \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) that
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_1\vee r_2.
 \tag{13}
\]

It remains to construct matching feasible tunings.  Put \(T=r_1\vee r_2=r_{\mathrm{np}}\).  Both exponents in (5) are strictly positive, so \(T\to0\).  The defining equalities
\[
 r_1^{1+d/(2\gamma)}=n^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 r_2^{1+A_*}=n^{-1}
\]
and \(T\ge r_1\vee r_2\) imply
\[
 n^{-1/2}T^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le T,
 \qquad
 n^{-1}T^{-A_*}\le T.
 \tag{14}
\]
Also, \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\ge n/4\) for \(n\ge12\).

Suppose first that \(q\ge\gamma\).  Choose
\[
 h=T^{1/\gamma},\qquad k=1,\qquad \ell=h.
 \tag{15}
\]
Eventually \(0<h\le r_0\), and
\[
 M=m h^d
 \ge\frac n4 T^{d/\gamma}
 \ge\frac n4 r_1^{d/\gamma}
 =\frac14 n^{2\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{16}
\]
Thus (15) belongs to \(\mathcal D_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Since eventually \(T\le1\), equations (2), (15), \(q\ge\gamma\), and \(\alpha>0\) give
\[
 B(h,1)
 =C_B\{T+T^{q/\gamma}+T^{1+\alpha/\gamma}\}
 \lesssim T.
 \tag{17}
\]
By (1), (14), and \(m\ge n/4\),
\[
 a\le2n^{-1/2}T^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le2T,
 \qquad b=M^{-1}=a^2\le4T^2.
 \tag{18}
\]
Substituting (18) into (3), and using that \(x\) is fixed and \(T\le1\), yields \(S(h,1,\eta)\lesssim T\).

Suppose now that \(0<q<\gamma\).  Define
\[
 h=T^{1/\gamma},\qquad \ell_0=T^{1/q},\qquad
 K=(h/\ell_0)^d=T^{d(1/\gamma-1/q)}.
 \tag{19}
\]
Here \(1/\gamma-1/q<0\), so \(K\to\infty\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), take \(k=\lfloor K\rfloor\).  Then \(K\ge2\), whence \(K/2\le k\le K\), and the resulting \(\ell=h k^{-1/d}\) satisfies
\[
 \ell_0\le\ell\le2^{1/d}\ell_0.
 \tag{20}
\]
The bandwidth and effective-sample conditions follow exactly as in (16), and \(k\) is a finite positive integer; these are all the conditions defining \(\mathcal D_n\).  In particular, no rank cap is needed.  Equations (2), (19)--(20), and \(\alpha>0\) give
\[
 B(h,k)
 \le C_B\left\{T+2^{q/d}T+2^{\alpha/d}T^{1+\alpha/q}\right\}
 \lesssim T.
 \tag{21}
\]
Furthermore, (1), (14), (20), and \(m\ge n/4\) imply
\[
 a\le2n^{-1/2}T^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le2T
 \tag{22}
\]
and
\[
 b=m^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}
 \le4n^{-1}T^{-d/(2\gamma)}T^{-d/(2q)}
 =4n^{-1}T^{-A_*}\le4T.
 \tag{23}
\]
Using (22)--(23) in (3), together with \(T\le1\), gives
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)
 \le C_S\{\sqrt{x}(a+b)+xa^2+x^{3/2}ab+x^2b^2\}
 \lesssim T.
 \tag{24}
\]

In both cases we have exhibited an element of \(\mathcal D_n\) whose objective is at most a constant multiple of \(T\).  Combining this upper bound with (10) and (13) proves
\[
 \inf_{\substack{0<h\le r_0,\ k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\\
                  m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)}}
 \{B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\}
 \asymp r_{\mathrm{np}}.
\]
